title: A Space-Weapons Card Came Out of the Box Called Counterspace
part1:
In military news about space, the most confusing thing is the words, not what the weapons can do.

A good example is “counterspace.” When you hear only the name, it sounds like putting attack weapons in outer space. But in fact, it is a much broader term.

According to the U.S. Space Force, counterspace operations include not only activities carried out in orbit, but also attacks and defense carried out through communication links and ground facilities.

In other words, this large box included work monitoring satellites, work supporting communications, activities carried out on the ground, work protecting satellites, and even weapons placed in space.
part2:
So, even if the U.S. Space Force says that it monitors satellites, helps provide location information, tracks missiles, and makes satellite systems harder to damage, that alone does not mean that it has “placed attack weapons in space.” These are missions to keep using satellites as basic infrastructure for the military and society.

But on September 14, a somewhat heavier card came out of that box.

The U.S. Secretary of the Air Force said that the United States is deploying space-control weapons in orbit to protect joint military forces from actions by hostile opponents.

An official article from a U.S. government agency recorded this statement as the first admission that the U.S. Space Force had deployed weapons in space.
part3:
Of course, the names and capabilities of the weapons were not announced. Their targets and methods of attack are unknown. What was made public here was not the details of the weapons, but the fact that weapons were being placed in orbit.

There have been cases of Russia destroying satellites with missiles fired from the ground. But those are attacks launched from the ground. They are a different matter from placing weapons in orbit.

The interesting point this time is not that the secrets of space warfare were suddenly revealed all at once. It is that, for the first time, a single card—“weapons deployed in space”—officially came out into the open from the overly broad box called counterspace.
in_one_line: For the first time, the United States officially admitted that it had deployed weapons in orbit.
